stories.title: WVU leads a $321 million energy and AI engine, with up to $160 million from NSF.
stories.html: The Resilient Energy Technology and Infrastructure Consortium, led by WVU with the University of Pittsburgh, Carnegie Mellon, and more than 60 regional partners, will receive up to $160 million from the National Science Foundation over ten years, plus $161 million from industry, workforce, philanthropy, state government, and community partners. In WVU's release, NSF RETI Engine CEO Erienne Olesh said the consortium will develop hardware, software, and AI technologies to help secure America's energy supply and strengthen the grid. It says the funding is projected to generate 21,000 jobs, 150 startups, and more than $1 billion in economic growth for the region. Those are projections, not results.

stories.title: WVU researchers are building AI into field sensors.
stories.html: With an NSF Early-Concept Grant for Exploratory Research, biologist Steve Kannenberg and postdoctoral researcher Jie Hu are building AI and very small on-site computers into environmental monitoring sensors, so scientists could see how ecosystems respond to droughts and wildfires in near real time instead of waiting months or years. The project also includes a plain-language AI chatbot for the data. The researchers plan to test the approach at sites in Colorado and Massachusetts.

stories.title: WVU offers an online M.S. in Artificial Intelligence.
stories.html: The Statler College of Engineering and Mineral Resources offers a 30-credit online M.S. in Artificial Intelligence: ten 8-week courses, asynchronous with synchronous office hours, with specialized tracks in machine learning or intelligent systems. The program page lists Fall, Spring and Summer starts, with the next start on January 11, 2027, and says the degree prepares graduates for careers in healthcare, cybersecurity, energy systems and intelligent automation.

stories.title: WVU plans a Strategic Compass seed funding initiative.
stories.html: President Benson is leading a seed funding initiative for innovative projects meant to turn ideas into action across the Strategic Compass priorities of education, discovery, health, service, and experiences. WVU says it will fully launch later this year and is seeking initial investors now, with a push during the Day of Giving on March 25, 2026.

stories.title: 1Mby1M says its virtual accelerator and AI Mentor can serve West Virginia founders.
stories.html: In a February 2026 blog post, 1Mby1M founder Sramana Mitra says West Virginia entrepreneurs can use the company's online, equity-free accelerator and AI Mentor for structured mentorship, global case studies, and frameworks for bootstrapping and scaling tech and tech-enabled services startups without relocating. The post is the company's own promotion and does not announce a West Virginia launch.

stories.title: Anurag Srivastava leads power and energy systems research at WVU.
stories.html: The Power Chair Professor in the Lane Department of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering leads power and energy systems research and teaching, including grid resilience against cyber and weather events and AI analytics for the power grid. His WVU profile says his projects have been supported by more than $66 million in funding from agencies and organizations such as the U.S. Department of Energy, the National Science Foundation, DARPA, and industry partners.
stories.dnote: Faculty profile page; no publication date.

stories.title: Data Driven WV pairs students with West Virginia organizations.
stories.html: Data Driven WV sits in the John Chambers College of Business and Economics, where Joshua Meadows is executive director. WVU Today says it connects West Virginia businesses, nonprofits, and community partners that need modern data and technology services with student consulting teams led by paid student Fellows.
stories.dnote: Center page; no publication date shown.

stories.title: WVU Board of Governors approves new program offerings in AI and smart systems.
stories.html: The Board of Governors approved a new online MS degree in Artificial Intelligence, housed in the Lane Department of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering. Statler College's roundup of new offerings also lists a graduate Digital Health certificate, new areas of emphasis including Artificial Intelligence and Computational Data Science and Cyber-Physical and Complex Systems, an undergraduate Artificial Intelligence area of emphasis, and two dual degrees pairing computer engineering or computer science with robotics engineering.

stories.title: WVU's F1Tenth team placed second at an IEEE international competition.
stories.html: The Statler College's Aug 1, 2025 report on new program offerings says WVU's AI-powered F1Tenth team, which builds an autonomous car, placed second in the previous year's Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers international competition.

stories.title: WVU AI Symposium 2025.
stories.html: The symposium program lists talks on dermatological image analysis with ChatGPT, AI design of anti-cancer and anti-bacterial peptides, learning algorithms for autonomous manufacturing, and using machine learning to support broadband equity and deployment in rural Appalachia.

stories.title: West Virginia partners with GATC on AI drug discovery for opioid use disorder.
stories.html: In March 2024, Gov. Jim Justice's office announced a partnership between the state and tech firm GATC West Virginia Inc. to integrate AI into pharmaceutical research aimed at opioid use disorder. The announcement recognizes a $5 million investment, approved by the West Virginia Economic Development Authority and the West Virginia Jobs Investment Trust board, to support GATC's research and development lab at the WVU Innovation Center. GATC's AI platform was used in preclinical animal studies of a non-opioid, non-habit-forming drug candidate, and the funding is meant to help GATC hire dozens of employees to complete FDA application efforts for it.

stories.title: NOAA announced a supercomputer, Rhea, for its Fairmont computing center.
stories.html: In September 2024 NOAA announced a $99 million investment in Rhea, a high-performance computer for its Environmental Security Computing Center in Fairmont. NOAA said it will strengthen the agency's AI and machine learning work on weather, ocean, and climate forecasting. The money comes from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and the Inflation Reduction Act. This entry reports the announcement. NOAA's computing-systems page lists Hera, Ursa, and Mercury at Fairmont and does not mention Rhea, so we have not confirmed whether Rhea is installed or running.

stories.title: Foundation CEO: NOAA's Fairmont facility is unlikely to feel federal layoffs.
stories.html: After new federal layoffs hit NOAA in February 2025, the president and CEO of the West Virginia High Technology Foundation, which developed the I-79 Technology Park, told WBOY he had not been made aware of any cuts at the NOAA facility there and would be surprised by any disruption, because the work is considered "mission critical." He said he does not speak for NOAA or the federal government. He also said the agency signed a new 20-year lease at the park in September 2024.

stories.title: NOAA awards $100 million to build Rhea, a new supercomputer for Fairmont.
stories.html: HPCwire carried NOAA's September 2024 announcement that $100 million had been awarded to General Dynamics Information Technology for Rhea, a high-performance computer to be installed in a new modular facility at the NOAA Environmental Security Computing Center in Fairmont. The article says Rhea will add about eight petaflops to NOAA's existing research computing capacity of 35 petaflops, for weather, climate, ocean and ecosystem prediction.

stories.title: NASA Katherine Johnson IV&V Facility.
stories.html: NASA lists more than 275 people at the Katherine Johnson IV&V Facility in Fairmont, home of NASA's Independent Verification and Validation Program, which NASA says assures the safety and success of software on its highest-profile missions.
stories.dnote: Facility profile; the page shows only an 'Updated' stamp, not a publication date.

stories.title: I-79 Technology Park and NOAA supercomputing.
stories.html: A 2022 West Virginia Executive profile describes three NOAA satellite ground stations and a NOAA supercomputer at the West Virginia High Technology Foundation's I-79 Technology Park. Foundation president Jim Estep said applying supercomputing and AI to NOAA's free weather data could help double a $7 billion commercial weather industry, and that he was negotiating to bring cloud providers' data centers to the park. These are his projections and hopes, not results.

stories.title: Thunkable's AI pilot gets about 120 West Virginia students building apps.
stories.html: In a pilot run with the State of West Virginia and supported by the Rockefeller Foundation, about 120 high school students in Monongalia, Kanawha, and Berkeley counties built an estimated 80 mobile apps with Thunkable's no-code app builder and its AI tools, and four schools completed the curriculum. Thunkable reports that 44% of students said they were more interested in starting a business. These figures come from Thunkable's own press release, which the Rockefeller Foundation posted.

sources.label: Thunkable pilot release, Rockefeller Foundation, Sep 10, 2026

stories.title: West Virginia is building a statewide AI training model for teachers.
stories.html: The West Virginia Department of Education is developing a train-the-trainer approach to AI professional learning, designed for a state of 55 counties and thousands of educators. Regional specialists will support local leaders known as AI Mountaineers, who will help deliver the training in their counties and schools. The department's professional learning initiative is called PAINT, for Pedagogical AI for New Teaching, and the broader plan has three levels: Pioneer, Trailblazer, and Ridge Climber. The Southern Regional Education Board's account of a podcast conversation with the department's AI coordinator says the model is still being implemented and its long-term outcomes remain to be seen. State Superintendent Michele Blatt wrote in testimony submitted to a U.S. House Education and Workforce subcommittee in February 2026 that the department provides ongoing professional development focused on the science of teaching with AI integration, which it calls PAiNT. We found no count of teachers trained.

sources.label: State Superintendent's written testimony, U.S. House Education and Workforce Committee, Feb 24, 2026

stories.title: Secretary of State's AI-powered knowledge center wins an international award.
stories.html: The Secretary of State's office says its Internal Knowledge Center, which integrates knowledge management and artificial intelligence into a single employee experience, earned a 2026 Merit Award at the International Association of Commercial Administrators' annual conference. The office is a repeat winner of the association's awards.

stories.title: Southern WV Community & Technical College wins $1.8 million to bring AI across the college.
stories.html: The U.S. Department of Education's Fund for the Improvement of Postsecondary Education (FIPSE) program funded a four-year AI Readiness and Capacity Initiative at the college, to bring AI into academic programs and student services.

sources.label: Southern WV Community & Technical College, Jan 13, 2026

stories.title: Morrisey unveils a 20-year data center plan.
stories.html: The Responsible Data Center Development Plan, announced Aug 11, 2026, lists seven key points, says the Data Economy Office will manage the 20-year plan, and calls for a Data Center Advisory Council on standards for noise, setbacks, site security and proximity to sensitive areas.

stories.title: WV Digital Government Summit returned to Charleston.
stories.html: State and local government leaders, sponsors, and technology partners were set to meet on October 29, 2026. The event page now lists the summit as complete. It describes the summit as a chance to explore new technologies, modernize operations and solve pressing challenges, from cybersecurity and AI to data governance and digital service delivery.

stories.title: Morrisey finishes 2026 bills: 12 vetoes, 10 unsigned.
stories.html: The Governor finished acting on the bills passed in the 2026 regular session. Separately, HB 4983, which approves the data center certification rule and keeps petitions confidential, became law, while bills to restore local control died.

stories.title: HB 4983 clears House 78-16: data-center confidentiality.
stories.html: The bill approves Morrisey administration rulemaking that would keep basic information about proposed high-impact data center projects confidential and hidden from public view. Seven Republicans joined all nine House Democrats in voting no, and opponents raised transparency concerns.

stories.title: Lawmakers reject efforts to restore local control over data centers.
stories.html: As of Feb. 25, 2026, the Senate president had not introduced a bill to revisit the data center rules, and a Senate bill that would largely restore local control had not been placed on a committee agenda. In the House, delegates voted down 87-6 an amendment that would have let residents within 10 miles of a project vote on it. The 2025 law that stripped counties and municipalities of the ability to enforce zoning, noise and light ordinances on data centers stayed in place.

stories.title: State AI Task Force works with WVOT on AI policy.
stories.html: The AI Task Force, established under §5A-6-9 of the WV Code, works with the WVOT cybersecurity office to develop policies and procedures for responsible AI use in state government. The Office of Technology's AI page posts task force meeting agendas, including one for January 23, 2026.

stories.title: S.O.LO: Secretary of State calls it the state's first agency AI chatbot.
stories.html: The Secretary of State's office launched an AI assistant, S.O.LO., that guides users through business registration and helps them find forms, filings and resources. In a Nov. 19, 2025 post, Secretary Kris Warner calls it West Virginia's first AI-powered chatbot developed and put into use by a state government agency, and says the office received the 2025 True Merit Award at the 48th Annual IACA Conference.

sources.label: Kris Warner (Secretary of State), via Bowles Rice, Nov 19, 2025

stories.title: OpenAI said it was looking at 16 states for Stargate sites, including West Virginia.
stories.html: In February 2025, OpenAI said it was looking at 16 states, including West Virginia, for sites for Stargate data centers. Stargate is a joint venture of OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank that said it is investing $100 billion, and eventually up to $500 billion. OpenAI said it plans somewhere between five and 10 campuses in total, and its request for proposals asked for sites near power and water infrastructure.

stories.title: TechConnect WV: supporting tech startups from the earliest stages.
stories.html: Based in South Charleston, TechConnect WV says it champions and supports tech entrepreneurship, starting with the earliest stages. It says it has spent more than 20 years enabling collaboration, research and scientific innovation.

stories.title: WVIAIS: AI consulting for small business.
stories.html: West Virginia Integrated AI Solutions focuses on making AI affordable for small businesses across the state, with a specialty in data entry and administrative automation.

stories.title: Marshall's medical school builds AI into training and clinics.
stories.html: The Joan C. Edwards School of Medicine says it is integrating AI across education, with adaptive-learning platforms and AI-assisted case generation for students. It describes clinical tools including an AI system that detects polyps during colonoscopies and an AI documentation assistant, alongside bioinformatics and AI research, including its Translational Bioinformatics and AI Innovations Lab.

sources.label: Marshall School of Medicine, "AI & Medicine," Mar 19, 2026

stories.title: Marshall plans an AI simulation pilot for counseling training.
stories.html: In January 2026 Marshall announced that its Department of Counseling had signed an agreement with Soma Lab Inc. (SimCare AI), a for-profit maker of AI-driven clinical simulation software, for design, a pilot program, and evaluation. Marshall said it would receive early access to the software beginning that spring, contribute faculty expertise, help gather user feedback, take part in pilot testing, and seek grant funding for a wider rollout. The announcement names no funding, and we have not confirmed the pilot's current status.

stories.title: Marshall builds a $45 million cybersecurity institute.
stories.html: Neighborgall Construction is building the $45 million, roughly 72,000-square-foot Institute for Cyber Security in Huntington, due to open in August 2027. It will hold advanced cyber ranges, digital forensics labs, unmanned-systems research space, and operational-technology environments. WSAZ reported in August 2026 that cyber defense work is already under way at several campus locations, and that Intuit launched a security operations center on campus in June.

sources.label: Marshall Institute for Cyber Security, "ICS Building Updates"

stories.title: Quality Insights gifts $1.2M to Marshall iCenter.
stories.html: The funding pays for a full-time gener8tor program manager in Huntington, two gBETA accelerator cohorts per year for three years, and one gALPHA cohort per year focused on ideation and early-stage testing in startups.

stories.title: Marshall University's AI governance.
stories.html: Marshall's AI governance began with the Presidential Task Force on AI, formed in 2023. That work now continues through an AI Steering Committee, with AI Enablement and Academic AI Integration sub-committees. Marshall offers students, faculty, and staff access to Coursera's Career Academy, with 6,000+ courses, through a license request.
stories.dnote: Living policy pages, first published Feb to Mar 2025 and updated since; no single publication date.

stories.title: IDEA District and the $45M Institute for Cyber Security.
stories.html: Marshall's IDEA District, first introduced as the Innovation District, is taking shape just west of the Huntington campus. It is anchored at one end by the $45 million, state-funded Institute for Cyber Security, now under construction, and at the other by the Brad D. Smith Center for Business and Innovation. Marshall says construction began in November and is expected to be completed in the summer of 2027.

stories.title: Marshall and Intuit announce a strategic partnership.
stories.html: Marshall and Intuit announced a partnership with three initiatives. One is a hiring funnel between Marshall and Intuit for tech-driven jobs like cybersecurity. Another is a prosperity hub planned for Marshall's Innovation District, where Intuit's David Graham said students would build tax, bookkeeping and AI skills through hands-on roles. The third is a plan to explore using Intuit's financial education curriculum with college and high school students.

stories.title: Marshall's first gBETA cohort.
stories.html: Five startups were chosen for the inaugural gBETA cohort at Marshall's iCenter: FarmerzTool Technology, get2there, Monarch Learning Labs, Quest R&D, and Stitch AI, with support from Huntington National Bank.

stories.title: Generation WV AI workforce panel.
stories.html: Josh Spence, chair of the WV Task Force on Artificial Intelligence and chief information officer at Alpha Innovations, spoke on an AI workforce panel at Generation West Virginia's Pathways to Progress conference, held May 8, 2025, in Charleston. In the organization's July 17, 2025 recap he is quoted: "AI is the priority." On infrastructure: "Broadband is not a nice-to-have. It is a must-have."

stories.title: Helsing plans a $50 million AI-enabled drone factory in Martinsburg.
stories.html: The Governor announced on July 13, 2026 that the German defense company Helsing will invest an initial $50 million in Berkeley County to make its HX-2 AI-enabled strike drone. The Governor's office says the plant will create at least 60 full-time jobs averaging $125,000 a year. Metro News reports that Helsing's U.S. general manager said the plant would produce 2,000 drones a month. The state developed a customized workforce training program with West Virginia Advance and Blue Ridge Community and Technical College. This is defense manufacturing, and the jobs and production figures are announced plans, not results.

stories.title: One year after HB 2014, state approvals show limits on environmental review and transparency.
stories.html: On the law's first anniversary, the Gazette-Mail reported that recent state approvals of data center projects in Mason and Putnam counties show tight limits on environmental protection and public transparency. In response to public comments on the Monarch stormwater permit, the DEP acknowledged that the permit does not require routine water sampling and does not consider cumulative impacts from multiple projects in a watershed. A Department of Commerce letter, obtained through a records request, said Commerce staff had held standing bi-weekly meetings with a Google affiliate about a Putnam County project for more than six months, with Appalachian Power and the county development authority present but not the public.

stories.title: Residents press for data center protections as projects move forward.
stories.html: West Virginia Watch reports that residents in Tucker, Mason, Berkeley and Mingo counties are pressing for more transparency and local say over data center projects, after lawmakers took no substantial action on safeguards this session. Residents raise concerns about water use, air pollution and health, noise and light, and energy rates, and say they are feeling the burn of "empty promises" from elected officials.

stories.title: $4 billion Penzance data center announced.
stories.html: Governor Morrisey announced a $4 billion private investment by Penzance Management at full buildout and said its Bedington Campus earned designation as West Virginia's first High Impact Intelligence Center. The campus will be on 548 acres in the Falling Waters District of Berkeley County and, at full buildout, will total approximately 1.9 million square feet and deliver 600 megawatts of critical IT capacity. The Governor's office says no state funding was used.

stories.title: Nscale takes over Monarch; Anthropic signs on.
stories.html: UK-based Nscale bought Fidelis-affiliated American Intelligence & Power Corp. (AIPCorp) in March 2026 and is developing the planned Monarch Compute Campus in Mason County. Its proposed 2.16 GW gas-fired microgrid is under DEP air review, and Nscale's S-1 says Anthropic agreed to payments of up to approximately $44.6 billion, subject to delivery and availability requirements, for GPU services at the campus. See Project Watch.

sources.label: WV DEP, public comment on the Monarch air permit

stories.title: HB 2014: Certified Microgrid Program.
stories.html: House Bill 2014, the Certified Microgrid Program, took effect July 11, 2025, ninety days after passage.

stories.title: Microgrid revenue reinvestment.
stories.html: Under the microgrid legislation, the Governor's office says, revenue generated from projects like Penzance's will be reinvested as follows: 50% to a Personal Income Tax Reduction Fund, 30% to the host county, 10% to all counties per capita, 5% to the Electric Grid Stabilization and Security Fund, and 5% to the Economic Enhancement Grant Program.

stories.title: Berkeley County asks the AG how HB 2014 preemption works. The AG declines.
stories.html: County officials sent a 10-page request about stormwater MS4 duties and public service districts under the state's data center law. AG J.B. McCuskey declined on Oct 9, citing ongoing and anticipated litigation, including the pending Barks lawsuit in Ohio County.

stories.title: PowerFlo Solutions plans a $20 million manufacturing site in Williamstown.
stories.html: PowerFlo Solutions, led by West Virginia native Jim Vuksic, will invest $20 million to establish advanced manufacturing operations in the 240,000-square-foot former Hino plant in Williamstown, the Governor's office announced. The Governor's release says the project will create between 120 and 200 full-time jobs, and Metro News reports at least 120. Metro News says the company, which is based in Marietta, Ohio, designs and builds electrical equipment for data centers and AI, such as power distribution units, static transfer switches, dry-type transformers, and custom control panels. The state made an adjacent 11-acre parcel available for expansion. The job figures are announced plans, not results.

stories.title: WVU-P Innovation and Technology Center opens.
stories.html: WVU-P invested nearly $35 million to turn the former Ohio Valley University campus in Vienna into its Innovation and Technology Center. Classes began in August 2025 with 159 students, including hands-on cybersecurity and networking work.

stories.title: Wheeling named among cities emerging with IT-enabled services ventures.
stories.html: 1Mby1M founder Sramana Mitra writes that Wheeling, Huntington and Martinsburg are "emerging with niche IT-enabled services ventures." Her post says founders in those cities can use 1Mby1M's equity-free virtual accelerator and AI Mentor to validate markets and plan growth.

stories.title: Form Energy reportedly lands $1B battery deal for Google data center.
stories.html: Form Energy's Weirton factory is set to build the iron-air batteries for a planned 300 MW / 30 GWh, 100-hour storage system, in a project with Xcel Energy, to help power a new Google data center in Minnesota. Tech Startups, citing The Information, reports a $1 billion commitment. The system is described as the largest battery ever announced by energy capacity, and WTRF reports it is Form's first deployment serving a data center. The plan still requires approval from the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission.

stories.title: Weirton plant targets 500 MW a year by 2028.
stories.html: Form Energy's Weirton factory, which will build the iron-air batteries for the Google and Xcel Energy project, is expected to reach 500 MW of annual production capacity by 2028.

stories.title: State education department moves to bring AI tools into classrooms.
stories.html: A Mercer County Schools technology integration specialist says the district has a state Department of Education guidance document on the use of AI in schools. WVVA reports the department intends to bring AI tools into classrooms, with teachers expected to use them for lesson plans and finding resources.

stories.title: Mercer County teachers attend AI assembly.
stories.html: Mercer County Public Schools teachers and faculty attended a back-to-school assembly focused on AI. According to the district, the assembly shared how AI can support educators' work.

stories.title: WVU Tech to host Governor's Computer Science Institute.
stories.html: The residential summer program is set to teach AI, coding, and drone programming to West Virginia 9th and 10th graders. WVU Tech will host it for three summers, starting in summer 2026 on the Beckley campus.

stories.title: WVU Tech president joins RNL's AI Leadership Council.
stories.html: President T. Ramon Stuart was appointed to Ruffalo Noel Levitz's AI Leadership Council. WVU Tech's announcement says the council's goal is to drive discussions that will shape the future of AI in higher education, and that members' insights will influence RNL's AI solutions.

stories.title: The FBI's biometrics center in Clarksburg marks ten years.
stories.html: The FBI's biometrics center opened in 2015 on the Criminal Justice Information Services Division campus in Clarksburg, a 360,000-square-foot facility. The FBI's anniversary story is mostly about fingerprint and iris systems. It says the algorithms for fingerprints, latent prints, face, and iris have each been upgraded, and it quotes an FBI assistant director crediting artificial intelligence for the accuracy of the fingerprint and iris algorithms.

stories.title: TekSynap acquires JBA, strengthening FBI tech support.
stories.html: The acquisition expands TekSynap's IT, cloud, and cyber support for FBI programs, including the CJIS Division in Clarksburg.

stories.title: FBI CJIS Division in Clarksburg.
stories.html: The secure 986-acre campus has about 3,500 employees and contractors, most in CJIS Main and the Biometric Technology Center.

stories.title: Appeals court dismisses Ridgeline permit appeals on jurisdiction; groups can take them to the state Supreme Court.
stories.html: In two orders filed Aug 26, the Intermediate Court of Appeals ruled that it lacks jurisdiction over the appeals by Tucker United, the WV Highlands Conservancy and the Sierra Club of the Air Quality Board's approval of the Ridgeline air permit, pointing to conflicting state statutes about where such appeals belong. The court noted the groups would have "good cause" to file late with the state Supreme Court of Appeals, which WTAP says clears the way for them to take the legal fight there. Ridgeline is a proposed 1,600-megawatt, off-grid gas-and-diesel power plant and data center being developed by Fundamental Data.

stories.title: Report projects $19M to $35M in health damages from the Ridgeline project in Tucker County.
stories.html: A report commissioned by Tucker United, a coalition that has opposed the project, and produced via the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health's Dominici lab estimates $19 million to $35 million in health-related damages if the expected Ridgeline operation runs as permitted. The Gazette-Mail obtained the report before its planned release.

stories.title: Groups appeal for blacked-out Ridgeline permit data.
stories.html: Citizen groups say emissions data and design details are blacked out in Fundamental Data's air permit application, and appealed to get the information released.
